title: Kenyan Roasted Maize
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Mahindi ya Kuchoma is Kenya's most iconic street food — whole maize cobs grilled slowly over glowing charcoal until the kernels are lightly charred, sweet, and smoky. Rubbed with lemon and chilli salt and eaten directly from the cob, it is the taste of every Kenyan roadside.
longDesc: No street food is more universally Kenyan than roasted maize. From Nairobi roundabouts to Mombasa beachfronts, the sight of a vendor turning maize cobs over charcoal is inseparable from the rhythm of daily life. The maize chars lightly at the edges, sweetens in the heat, and takes on a smoky depth that no other cooking method can replicate. Rubbed with a cut lemon dipped in salt and chilli, it becomes something extraordinary.
steps: Light the charcoal and allow to burn until fully covered with white ash — glowing coals, not open flames.
Place the husked maize cobs directly on the grill grate over medium charcoal heat.
Grill for 15—20 minutes, turning every 3—4 minutes, until the kernels are cooked through with light char marks on all sides.
Mix the salt and chilli powder together on a small plate.
Dip the cut lemon half into the salt and chilli mixture.
Rub the lemon generously over the hot maize cob, squeezing as you go.
Rub with butter if desired. Serve immediately.
chefTips: Use fresh maize for the best natural sweetness — slightly underripe cobs with plump, milky kernels are ideal.
Cook over medium coals, not fierce heat — slow roasting sweetens the maize without burning it.
The lemon-salt-chilli rub is the entire experience — do not skip it.
commonMistakes: Cooking over open flames — burns the outside while the inside stays raw.
Using overripe maize — becomes starchy and tough rather than sweet.
storage: Best eaten immediately from the grill.
reheating: Not recommended — roasted maize is only good fresh.
healthBenefits: Good source of fibre, vitamin C, and B vitamins.
Low in fat when eaten without butter.
culturalNote: Roasted maize is woven into Kenyan street culture. The sight of a maize vendor turning cobs over glowing charcoal at the roadside is one of the most universally familiar images in Kenyan daily life — enjoyed by schoolchildren, office workers, and market traders alike.
regionalVariations: With butter and chilli — popular in Nairobi.

faqs.q: Can I roast maize on a gas grill?
faqs.a: Yes, though charcoal gives the authentic smoky flavour. On a gas grill, use high heat and char slightly on all sides.

cookingScience: Roasting maize over charcoal causes the Maillard reaction on the kernel surfaces, creating hundreds of new flavour compounds that give the characteristic smoky, caramelised taste.
sustainabilityTips: Buy fresh maize from local farmers.
Maize husks and cobs are compostable.
